title: Linguistic Foundations for Constructing Speech Synthesis in the Kazakh Language
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of correctly recognizing and pronouncing, in accordance with orthoepic norms, shortened words and abbreviations, numerical symbols, mathematical operations, formulas, and conventional signs within the Kazakh-language text-to-speech system. The main objective of the study is to identify the linguistic features of fully expanding shortened words and abbreviations in texts processed by the speech synthesis system, as well as of representing mathematical expressions in written form, and on this basis to develop a linguistic resource that ensures natural, consistent, and realistic synthesized speech in Kazakh. The article clarifies the distinction between shortened words and abbreviations and proposes several approaches to incorporating them into a speech synthesis program. In particular, it describes methods such as compiling comprehensive lists of shortened forms from domain-specific texts, presenting shortened and full variants in parallel, and preserving internationally established abbreviations in their original forms. The article also provides a dedicated phonetic transcription of shortened words and demonstrates their pronunciation in complia

title: Deep Learning Principles Meet Translanguaging: Opportunities, Challenges, and Pedagogical Pathways for Indonesian Secondary Education
abstract: This research aims to explore the integration of deep learning (DL) and translanguaging in the context of English Language Teaching (ELT) in Indonesia, with a focus on the opportunities, challenges, and pedagogical pathways that arise in classroom practice. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis. Data analysis was carried out using an interactive model by Miles et al. (2014) that included data condensation, data presentation, and conclusion/verification. The findings of the study show that translanguaging contributes to encouraging mindful learning through increased student metacognitive awareness, meaningful learning through connections with local contexts and student experiences, and joyful learning through increased emotional engagement and active participation. However, implementation also faces various challenges, including rigid curriculum limitations, low teacher readiness, and complexity in classroom management. title: Balinese Youth’s Understanding of Traditional Balinese Food Lexicons: An Eco-Linguistic and Traditional Literature Perspective
abstract: This study aims to identify lexicons related to traditional Balinese food and cooking utensils. The method used is a mixed method with an exploratory sequential design. Qualitative data were collected through interviews with 18 traditional leaders in eight regencies in Bali. Quantitative data were collected through tests administered to 320 elementary school students (160 from urban and 160 from rural areas) to assess their understanding of the lexicon. Qualitative data were analyzed using an interactive analysis model, while quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and an independent t-test. The qualitative data analysis revealed 126 lexicons related to traditional Balinese food. The lexicon was dominated by nouns, followed by verbs and adjectives. Quantitative data analysis revealed a significant difference in understanding between students in rural and urban areas, indicating that residence location influences understanding. Although the difference in understanding levels was significant, their understanding was still considered low overall. title: The Impact of Generative AI Chatbots on Saudi EFL Students’ Productive Vocabulary Development and Learner Autonomy: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction has generated increasing interest, particularly in relation to vocabulary learning and learner autonomy. However, empirical evidence on their impact on productive vocabulary development remains limited, especially in the EFL context in the Middle East. This study investigated the impact of a generative AI chatbot on Saudi EFL students' productive vocabulary development and learner autonomy. Employing a quasi-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design, data were collected from 30 undergraduate EFL learners over a four-week instructional intervention. Participants completed a productive vocabulary test before and after the intervention, and a learner autonomy questionnaire at the end of the study. Paired-samples t-test results revealed statistically significant improvement in the students’ productive vocabulary performance following the chatbot-supported intervention. Descriptive analysis of the questionnaire responses indicated generally positive perceptions of learner autonomy, particularly in goal setting, strategy use, self-monitoring, and responsibility fo

title: University EFL Students’ Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education Learning Environments
abstract: This study explores university EFL students’ perceptions of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education learning environments, particularly within Faculty of Teacher Training and Education in Indonesia. Employing a qualitative phenomenological design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with nine students from the Faculty of Teacher Training and Education who actively use AI-assisted tools in their academic activities. The findings reveal that EFL students demonstrate high familiarity with AI applications, especially for language learning, doing tasks, and perceive AI as a supportive learning assistant that enhances efficiency, autonomy, and confidence. AI tools are widely valued for providing immediate feedback, facilitating comprehension, and reducing learning anxiety through flexible and interactive learning experiences. However, the study also identifies critical concerns related to accuracy, ethical integrity, and dependency, as excessive reliance on AI may hinder critical thinking and academic responsibility. These findings highlight the dual role of AI as both an empowering pedagogical resource and a potential challenge when used uncritically. The stu

title: AI Harnessing in Language Learning: A Systematic Review of Opportunities for Innovation and Pedagogical Transformation
abstract: This research presents a systematic review of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in language education, synthesising evidence on tools used for teaching and learning. The review encompassed empirical, conceptual and review studies identified from key education and language databases and is focused on AI use by language learners and teachers in both formal and non-formal contexts. The review is organised under five main dimensions: (1) stakeholder perceptions and readiness; (2) AI applications and associated technologies; (3) AI tools’ impact on language skills and affective factors; (4) pedagogical integration and instructors’ professional development; and (5) overall affordances/challenges and the future implications. The findings reveal that generative AI and conversational agents are increasingly becoming integral components in language education, utilised by educators to offer personalised feedback, adaptive practice, and student engagement and motivation. Evidence also indicates positive impacts regarding writing quality, oral performance, vocabulary, and academic motivation. title: Sound-Meaning Correspondence and Child-Directed Speech in Early Language Development: Evidence From Kazakh Caregiver Speech
abstract: This study examines the phonological, semantic, and communicative features of caregiver speech and children’s self-created words in early language development, based on data from Kazakh-speaking families. The research is based on a survey of 50 parents and explores two key aspects: (1) the use of terms of endearment in child-directed speech, and (2) children’s spontaneous formation of novel words associated with object properties. The results show that nearly half of the respondents use non-standard, phonologically simplified expressions when addressing children, alongside traditional lexical forms. These expressions are characterized by reduplication, elongated intonation, and simple syllabic structures, and primarily convey emotional closeness, softness, and smallness. In addition, the findings reveal that children actively create their own lexical items (e.g., titi, buba, kiki), which systematically reflect sound–meaning associations. In particular, front vowels and high-frequency consonants tend to be associated with smallness and sharpness, whereas back vowels and labial consonants are linked to largeness and softness. title: E-Portfolios for Reflective Practice Among Pre-Service EFL Teachers: A Qualitative Case Study in Vietnam
abstract: This qualitative case study examines how 17 pre-service English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers at a public university in Vietnam engaged with e-portfolios as a tool for reflective practice within a compulsory Teaching Methodology course. Drawing on Gibbs’ Reflective Cycle (1988) as a pedagogical scaffold, participants produced weekly reflective entries across an eight-week course. Data were generated from 136 e-portfolio entries and semi-structured interviews with all 17 participants and were analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2021). Three interrelated themes emerged. First, participants perceived e-portfolios positively as spaces for self-monitoring and professional identity formation, although initial unfamiliarity with reflective writing led to a subset to approach the task instrumentally. Second, Gibbs’ Cycle shaped the trajectory of reflective writing: entries moved from predominantly descriptive to increasingly analytical over time, with the Action Plan stage emerging as the most pedagogically productive, and the Feelings stage appeared to be the least elaborated. title: A Multimodal Analysis of BBC Reports on the Israel-Gaza War
abstract: This study suggests that multimodal discourse analysis is a valuable method for examining portrait-based BBC news reports. However, there is insufficient exploration of how portraits are structured and function alongside their accompanying texts, particularly in shaping portrayals of refugees. To address this, the research employs a qualitative approach, conducting a multimodal analysis of the BBC’s image-based coverage of the Israel-Gaza conflict that began on October 7, 2023. The analysis integrates both visual and textual perspectives to investigate the depiction of displaced Palestinians. The visual component applies Kress and Van Leeuwen’s (2006) visual design grammar framework, emphasizing interactional and compositional elements. The textual analysis, meanwhile, utilizes Halliday and Matthiessen’s (2004) transitivity framework. Findings from the visual analysis highlight how visual elements are used to positively frame displaced Palestinian Gazans, fostering global empathy and support. title: Assessing the National and Labor-Market Needs for Establishing a Bachelor’s Program in Teaching English to Young Learners (TEYL) in Jordan
abstract: The rapid growth of English teaching in Jordan has created a need for teachers with specialized pedagogical skills for young children. Most current undergraduate programs focus on language and literature. This study assesses the demand for a Bachelor's degree in Teaching English to Young Learners (TEYL) in Jordan to inform the development of a new program. title: Phatic Norms in Kazakh and English Digital Discourse: Cultural Code and Pragmatic Function
abstract: This article examines how phatic norms in Kazakh and English are condensed in the shift from face-to-face interaction to digital communication while preserving culturally specific meanings. It focuses on brief confirmations, forms of address, gratitude formulas, apologies, emojis, and other signals that sustain social connection. The topic is relevant because these markers are often interpreted differently in multilingual online environments, creating misunderstanding and latent tension. This is especially significant in international work teams, online education, and AI-mediated interaction, where recognition of phatic norms is essential. The study identifies similarities and differences in Kazakh and English phatic strategies used to open interaction, confirm participation, shape interpersonal effect, and close communication politely, while revealing the cultural codes underlying these practices. The material includes traditional communicative data, such as biys’ discourse, oratorical speech, and literary dialogues, together with digital data from messaging platforms, social networks, and workplace chats. title: The Impact of GenAI-Synthesia-Assisted Intercultural Communicative Language Teaching (ICLT) Model on Japanese Language and Intercultural Communication Competence
abstract: Japanese language competency interventions have not accommodated cultural competency, resulting in learners lacking adequate Japanese cultural knowledge. The purpose of this study was to investigate the impact of the GenAI-Synthesia-assisted Intercultural Communicative Language Teaching (ICLT) model on Japanese language and cultural competency. The research method used in this study was a quasi-experimental one involving 200 Japanese language learners from prospective Indonesian migrant workers who will work in Japan. The instruments used were the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT), an oral Japanese language competency test, an intercultural competency test, and a semi-structured group interview. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired-sample t-tests. The results of the study show that the GenAI-Synthesia-assisted ICLT model is able to improve Japanese language competence in written, oral, and intercultural communication. Improvements in written Japanese language competency were seen in the aspects of reading, writing, listening, grammar, letter recognition, and vocabulary. title: ‘Being Present’ Online: International Students’ Experiences of Social Presence in Pre-Sessional English Programmes in UK Higher Education
abstract: Online education has acquired an ever-increasing popularity since the onset of COVID-19, and the number of students studying online is rising, especially in Pre-sessional English programmes. These programmes serve as a transitional phase to support international students from diverse cultural and educational backgrounds as they pursue their postgraduate studies in the UK. This research aims to explore the impact of social presence on students’ learning in online learning classes. The study investigated affective, interactive and cohesive factors on students’ learning engagement and satisfaction. The study employed qualitative methods, conducting eight focus groups with students (n=44) from two British universities. In addition, an analysis of Independent Study Journals of 12 students was conducted to investigate participants’ learning behaviours and reflections. The findings demonstrate that tutor presence and course design often shape social presence rather than the reverse. Participants reported stronger connections with peers than with the tutor; however, they acknowledged the tutor’s supportive role in facilitating learning and establishing a sense of presence in the online env

title: A Discursive and Comparative Analysis of Phytonymic Symbols: Roses in English Folk Songs and Tulips in Kazakh Folk Songs
abstract: The purpose of this study is to identify symbolic models in the discourse of English and Kazakh folk song texts and to demonstrate their common and distinctive features. To determine the study’s theoretical conclusions and directions, I identified the concepts of "discourse" and "song discourse" the differences between text and discourse are presented in tabular form. The phytonym symbols of roses and tulips, characteristic of the two linguocultures, were chosen as the research material. From the discourse of the English folk songs, a discursive analysis of 14 rose lexemes was conducted, and eight symbolic models were identified. From the discourse of the Kazakh folk songs, 22 tulip lexemes were analyzed, and six symbolic models were identified. The symbolic models were analyzed, common and distinctive features characteristic of the two linguocultures were identified, and conclusions were drawn.

title: Assessing the Efficacy of AI-Powered Writing Prompts in Enhancing Students’ Writing Skills
abstract: The quantitative study examines the effectiveness of artificial intelligence writing prompts in teaching English for Specific Purposes (ESP) to 221 students from technical disciplines. The survey findings indicated that between 60% and 70% of respondents found the prompts readable and helpful for improving their writing and for receiving feedback. However, only 54.8% of participants strongly supported the diversity of prompts. Structured activities were perceived as the most beneficial, specifically narrative reviews (68.8%), slang exercises (68.3%), and essay completions (65.1%). Sixty-one percent to seventy-five percent of students reported perceived improvements in their capabilities, with 74.2% indicating that their confidence and attitudes towards writing were enhanced. The research confirms that AI is an effective tool for structured writing activities in line with the principles of Vygotskian education. However, AI's potential to encourage creative activities is limited, underscoring the importance of further human-centered instruction. title: Linguistic Features of AI-Based Legal Discourse: Evidence From LegalExpert.kz
abstract: This study examines the linguistic features of legal responses generated by artificial intelligence on the LegalExpert.kz platform. The aim of the research is to identify structural patterns at the lexical, syntactic, and pragmatic levels of such responses. The dataset consists of 50 user queries on actual legal issues in Kazakhstan and the corresponding AI-generated answers. The findings demonstrate that, at the lexical level, legal terms such as “court,” “case,” “evidence” and “document” occur with high frequency and form the semantic core of the texts. At the syntactic level, responses are structured according to predefined templates, with a noticeable predominance of conditional constructions (e.g., “if… then…”). This reflects the linguistic realization of the legal reasoning model “situation–condition–consequence”. At the pragmatic level, the responses are user-oriented, action-guiding, and express modality related to probability and caution. In addition, the results reveal a blending of legal discourse with everyday language. This indicates that AI-generated texts are adapted to make complex legal information accessible to a broad audience. The study contributes to understand

title: Teacher Self-Efficacy and Contextual Factors in Deep-Surface Instruction in EFL Teaching
abstract: Teacher self-efficacy is widely recognized as an important psychological construct influencing instructional quality in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms. However, limited research has examined how self-efficacy relates specifically to deep and surface instructional orientations while considering the role of contextual factors. This study investigates the relationship between EFL teachers’ self-efficacy and their instructional practices and examines whether contextual variables influence instructional orientation directly or through self-efficacy. A quantitative survey design was employed involving 104 English teachers from elementary, junior high, and senior high schools. Data were collected using the Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale (TSES) and the Approaches to Teaching Inventory (ATI) and analyzed using logistic regression techniques. The findings reveal that teacher self-efficacy significantly predicts instructional orientation, with teachers who report higher self-efficacy being substantially more likely to implement deep instructional practices rather than surface approaches. title: Investigating Saudi EFL Learners’ Engagement With ChatGPT Feedback Across Different Essay Genres
abstract: While the number of studies on learners’ engagement with ChatGPT feedback has recently increased, little attention has been paid to whether and how this engagement varies across different genres of essays, particularly in the context of EFL. To address this significant gap, this study employed a mixed-methods, case-study approach to investigate the engagement of six Saudi EFL learners with ChatGPT-generated feedback across three essay genres: opinion, narrative, and process. Data were collected through written drafts, reflection-on-mistakes (RM) worksheets, questionnaires, and semi-structured interviews, and were analyzed to examine behavioral, cognitive, and affective engagement. The results revealed significant differences across writing genres in terms of feedback quantity, genre, and uptake rate. Opinion essays received the most feedback, predominantly at the macro-level, whereas narrative and process essays received mainly micro-level feedback. The participants showed higher overall engagement with narrative and process essays than with opinion essays. title: Language as a Reflection of Buddhist and Brahmanical-Hindu Culture in the Thai Translation of Journey to the West
abstract: This study aims to examine language related to Buddhism and Brahmanical-Hinduism and to explore how such language reflects and constructs cultural meanings embedded within religious belief systems in the Thai translation of Journey to the West. The data were character names, honorific expressions, and symbolic lexical items associated with religious concepts, and were analyzed through semantic analysis within a framework of cultural reflection. The findings indicate that Journey to the West employs language not merely as a narrative device, but as a significant ideological mechanism for systematically conveying religious doctrines, moral values, and cosmological structures. With regard to Buddhist vocabulary, the text prominently features terms and proper names rooted in Mahayana Buddhist concepts across two dimensions: 1) Dhamma language and Buddhist terminology, such as 悟 (Wu / Ngo), meaning enlightenment or awakening; and 2) characters embodying Buddhism, such as Phra Thang Samjang (Tripitaka), who embodies the ideal of a morally disciplined monk. title: Creative Subtitling of Humor in Arabic: A Case Study of Friends Series
abstract: The subtitling of humor presents a significant challenge in audiovisual translation as it demands of the translator both linguistic skills and cultural understanding of the language pair involved. This study aimed to (i) identify the obstacles that translators encounter in the translation of humor in Friends into Arabic, and, (ii) the strategies used to accommodate the target viewers' cultural sensibilities. Nida’s framework was employed in this study to examine the subtitles. The dataset comprised a corpus of popular scenes whose humorous content was classified and the subtitles were evaluated by professional translators to identify problem areas and examine the efficacy of translation strategies used in the subtitles. The findings indicated that situational and character-based humor was mostly transferred successfully across languages while linguistic humor and culture-specific jokes could not be rendered as effortlessly. The study concluded with the observation that effective subtitling depends on flexible strategy selection while keeping in mind functional adequacy and cultural sensitivity of the audience. title: Proverbs as Inference Architecture: Projected Obligation, Humour, and Defeasibility in English and Vietnamese
abstract: This article models proverb use as an inference architecture: a conventionalised form–function configuration through which recognisable proverbial form compresses reasoning, invokes collective authority, and projects accountable uptake. Although paremiological and pragmatic accounts show that proverbs are culturally dense and contextually interpretable, they less fully specify how proverb form organises default inference and shapes alignment. Drawing on a controlled English–Vietnamese corpus of 300 proverb-as-utterance templates and a contextualised vignette subcorpus of 40 three-turn sequences, the study examines heuristic type, inferential target, alignment outcome, humour uptake, and defeasibility. Because the data are controlled and author-constructed rather than naturalistic, the analysis is exploratory and model-building. The findings suggest that projected obligation is most visible in advice and warning contexts, that epistemic and deontic alignment are separable, and that humorous uptake is associated with mixed alignment rather than immediate deontic closure. title: A Comprehensive Study of Linguistic, Cognitive, and Pedagogical Challenges in Learning Spanish as a Second Language Among Non-Native Adult Learners
abstract: This study examines adult learners’ written output of Spanish as a second language (L2), focusing on grammatical density, morphosyntactic complexity, and the correlation between the output and cognitive processing requirement. It employs a multilayered corpus that comprises a more reduced L2 learner corpus, a controlled Spanish baseline corpus and a larger global Spanish reference corpus. This allows descriptive as well as inferential analysis between various levels of proficiency, first-language status, task type, years of education, stay length in a non-native country, and first-exposure age. The findings display that adults’ written production in L2 is fairly high in grammatical density, reflecting a high dependence on explicit morphosyntactic encoding. This grammatical density improves with proficiency, showing structural integration and syntactic embedding at higher proficiency levels. There is consistent variation among L1 groups, which indicates the influence of typological transfer. title: Visualizing Medical Terminology: Effects of Sketchnoting on EMP Vocabulary Retention and Self-Regulated Learning Among Military Medical Cadets in Vietnam
abstract: This study examined whether sketchnoting improves English for Medical Purposes (EMP) vocabulary learning and self-regulated learning (SRL) at a military medical university in Vietnam. A total of 180 third-year cadets were allocated to an experimental group, trained in pen-and-paper sketchnoting, or a control group using traditional linear notes during a nine-week EMP module. Learning outcomes were measured through three EMP tests, an SRL and learning mechanisms questionnaire, a sketchnoting quality rubric, and semi-structured interviews. The two groups were equivalent at baseline in age, prior general English proficiency, and EMP pre-test scores. The experimental group significantly outperformed the control group on both immediate and delayed EMP tests, showing very large effect sizes and a much flatter forgetting curve across the four-week delay. Only the experimental group showed substantial gains in SRL (Planning, Monitoring, and Note and Review), and the Note and Review component correlated strongly with delayed EMP scores. title: Application of Self-Assessment Checklists in Supporting IELTS Writing Improvement for Advanced Learners: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of using guided self-assessment checklists to improve IELTS Writing performance among advanced learners, particularly those at around band 6.5. A quasi-experimental mixed-methods design was adopted, involving 75 participants divided into an experimental group (n = 37) and a control group (n = 38). Over an eight-week period, the experimental group engaged in a structured feedback cycle that incorporated self-assessment checklists, peer feedback, and teacher input, while the control group received only teacher feedback. The findings indicate that learners in the experimental group made noticeably greater improvements in writing performance compared to those in the control group. The most notable gains were observed in Task Response and Coherence and Cohesion, with a higher proportion of students reaching band 7.0 or above. Qualitative data further suggest that the intervention enhanced learners’ metacognitive awareness, goal-setting practices, and sense of autonomy. title: A Contrastive Pragmatic Analysis of Context-Dependent Meanings in English and Vietnamese Proverbs
abstract: Proverbs are often treated as fixed carriers of folk wisdom, yet their meanings in discourse are neither fully stable nor self-contained. This article investigates the context-dependent meanings of English and Vietnamese proverbs from a contrastive pragmatic perspective. Drawing on scholarship in paremiology, pragmatics, intercultural pragmatics, and contrastive analysis, the study examines how proverbs in the two languages generate meanings beyond their literal wording through contextual inference, indirect speech-act realization, and culturally embedded communicative norms. The study adopts a qualitative, literature-based, and contrastive design grounded in established proverb collections and foundational works in pragmatics and proverb studies. The analysis focuses on four dimensions: the shift from literal meaning to contextual meaning, the communicative functions of proverbs in discourse, the role of indirectness and inference, and pragmatic equivalence or non-equivalence across English and Vietnamese. The findings suggest that proverbs in both languages function as highly compressed pragmatic resources for advising, warning, criticizing, persuading, and justifying. At the sam

title: The Dynamics of Indonesian Language Use Among Students of Ensino Secundario São Pedro School, Dili, Timor-Leste
abstract: For approximately 24 years since Timor-Leste gained independence, the Indonesian language has continued to play a significant role in education, social communication, cross-border interactions, media, and access to literature in Timor-Leste. However, the extent to which Indonesian is still used and constitutes part of the linguistic identity of Timor-Leste’s younger generation has not been extensively examined, particularly within the context of secondary education. This study aims to describe the dynamics of Indonesian language use among students of Ensino Secundario São Pedro School, Dili, Timor-Leste. Employing a descriptive quantitative and qualitative approach, the study collected data through questionnaires, interviews, and speech analysis involving 30 student respondents. The findings indicate that the linguistic practices of students at Ensino Secundario São Pedro, Dili reflect adaptive, function-oriented multilingualism, in which Tetun–Portuguese code-mixing functions as a dominant marker of linguistic identity across domains, while Indonesian is used situationally to meet cross-community communication needs and specific academic purposes. title: Costuming Language: Dialect, Whiteness, and Power in Frank Yerby's The Foxes of Harrow
abstract: This study analyses the debut novel of Frank Yerby, The Foxes of Harrow (1946), by focusing on the dialect and linguistic politics, and placing the novel within broader discussions on linguistic purity, race, and cultural hegemony of the nineteenth century. Despite Yerby being currently one of the most commercially successful African American novelists of the twentieth century, there is an exceptionally narrow spectrum of critical interest in his fictional work. Based on the historical background of the Gilded Age, which saw an influx of anxieties about dialect and linguistic contamination with the ebb and flow of immigrant influx and the introduction of cultural pluralism, the present research posits that Yerby uses dialect as a strategic tool of resistance against the demand to have a standardized and cultivated American language. Yerby challenges the perceived notions of whiteness through the portrayal of Irish, Creole, and Black voices, clarifying the role of language as an indicator of privilege and an institutionalized place of exclusion at the same time. title: A Comparative Assessment of ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Human Translations of Cultural References in the Moroccan Novel For Bread Alone
abstract: The translatability of cultural references (CRs) has been a major problem for human translators, let alone artificial intelligence (AI) tools. This study evaluates the effectiveness of AI vis-à-vis human translations of CRs. The dataset was mined from For Bread Alone, a unique Arabic literary autobiographical masterpiece by the Moroccan author Mohamed Choukri (2000) and translated into English (1983) by Paul Bowles. The AI English translations were generated by Chat GPT (GPT) and DeepSeek (DS), Western vs Eastern AI systems. 300 English renderings of 100 CRs were analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively. The AI translations were assessed using BLEU, METEOR and chrF metrics vis-à-vis the human translation (HT), then both AI translations and HT were evaluated using Pedersen’s (2011) taxonomy of strategies (with two added strategies specifically used for this study). BLEU produced the highest results, while METEOR and chrF scores were significantly lower, and GPT scores were higher than DS in comparison to HT. The analysis of the strategies indicates that both GPT and DS relied heavily on source language oriented strategies, while HT made more use of target language oriented ones. Th

title: Noun-Adjective Agreement in Najdi Arabic: A Constraint-Based Account
abstract: Agreement is a cross-linguistic phenomenon that interestingly interacts with different language disciplines such as morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics. It has been investigated considerably in various linguistic topics in Standard Arabic. This, however, does not apply to modern Arabic varieties whose use is increasing nowadays. Najdi Arabic (NA) is an example of these Arabic varieties, where agreement has not received the same level of attention. Hence, the current paper focuses on a detailed investigation of one of the intriguing topics in agreement. It particularly explores the patterns of noun-adjective agreement in NA. Employing naturally occurring examples, the paper demonstrates how nominal variation correlates with adjectival agreement patterns. In addition to describing all noun-adjective agreement patterns, the paper provides a formal theoretical analysis of these patterns within the constraint-based approach of Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar (HPSG). title: Exploring the Development of AI-Mediated Competence for Sustainable Translation and Interpreting Education: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence has become increasingly central to translation and interpreting education, shaping classroom practice, feedback, assessment, and professional preparation. Yet the literature remains fragmented across work on machine translation, computer-assisted translation, post-editing, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, large language models, and AI-supported assessment. This bibliometric review examines how research in this area has developed from 2014 to May 2026, with particular attention to the movement from tool-oriented technology training toward AI-mediated competence. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus and analysed using VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The analysis focuses on publication trends, collaboration patterns, keyword co-occurrence, thematic clusters, and keyword bursts. The results show limited output before 2018, steady growth between 2019 and 2021, and rapid expansion after 2022. The keyword evidence points to a shift from machine translation, post-editing, and translation technology training toward AI literacy, evaluative judgement, output verification, feedback practices, ethical responsibility, professional agenc

title: Proverbs as Argumentative Strategy in Egyptian Arabic: A Sociopragmatic Study
abstract: This study examines the argumentative function of proverbs in the daily communication of Egyptians via a sociopragmatic perspective. The proverbs were pragmatically analyzed to reveal their implicature and to evaluate their communicative efficacy as an argumentative strategy. Moreover, the proverbs were socially analyzed to determine whether social variables such as age, gender, education, and place of residence influence their frequency. To conduct this study, fifty-two common proverbs were collected through close observation, note-taking, TV soap operas, films, social media, and the repertoire. Leech’s (1983) Interpersonal Rhetoric Model, Austin’s (1975), and Searle’s (1969, 1976) Speech Act Theory were used to analyze the pragmatic import of each proverb. The study showed that older people, particularly women, villagers, slum dwellers, and laypersons, frequently use proverbs because they are simple, ready-made, and authoritative argumentative strategies. In contrast, youth, highly educated people, and residents of upscale districts rarely use proverbs for social reasons. title: Exploring AI-Assisted Translation and Cognitive Load in L2 Learning: Evidence From Indonesian University Students
abstract: This study examines the role of AI-assisted translation in second language learning among Indonesian university students, with particular attention to cognitive load, engagement, feedback literacy, and perceived translation quality. Adopting a mixed-methods design, the research combined quantitative data from 217 students with qualitative insights from 12 semi-structured interviews involving learners from six language programs, including English, German, Arabic, Mandarin, Korean, and Japanese. The quantitative findings showed that all three measured constructs were rated at high levels, and the questionnaire subscales demonstrated satisfactory reliability, with Cronbach’s alpha values above 0.80. Students generally perceived AI-assisted translation as beneficial for reducing surface-level difficulties, especially in vocabulary selection, grammatical accuracy, and task completion speed. At the same time, the findings revealed that the tool did not eliminate mental effort, as students still needed to verify, evaluate, and revise AI-generated outputs carefully. The interview data added further depth by showing that AI-assisted translation was valued for improving efficiency and confid

title: Beyond Phonetic Adaptation: Reanalysis and Multimodal Reframing of “VAR” in Arabic Digital Football Discourse
abstract: This study examines the reanalysis of the acronym ‘VAR’ (‘video assistant referee’) in Arabic football discourse, focusing on how it is transformed into a culturally loaded symbol in digital communication. While prior research has addressed phonological adaptation, emoji use, and Arabic digital discourse separately, little attention has been paid to how these processes interact in real-time meaning construction. This study addresses this gap by investigating how ‘VAR’, realized in English as a spelled-out acronym (V-A-R), is lexicalized in Arabic as /far/, enabling its reinterpretation as ‘fār’ (‘mouse’). This reinterpretation is not purely phonological but is constructed and circulated through multimodal resources, particularly emojis and sarcastic hashtags such as ‘taqniyyat_alfār’ (‘VAR technology’) and ‘ḥakam_alfār’ (‘VAR referee’), which index humor, criticism, and mistrust. Drawing on a dataset of Arabic tweets from the Roshn Saudi League 2025-2026, the analysis shows how this form develops a dual function: retaining its technical reference while simultaneously operating as a shared symbolic critique. The findings demonstrate that meaning in Arabic digital discourse emerges t

title: Enhancing University Students’ Speaking Skills Through Debate-Based Instruction: A Classroom Action Research Study
abstract: The study aims to explore the effectiveness of debate activities as an instructional method for improving the speaking competencies of non-English major students in a Vietnamese university context, addressing the gap in process-oriented research on debate-based instruction in Vietnamese tertiary EFL contexts. The study employed the Classroom Action Research (CAR) design with 20 first-year students across two instructional cycles. The class observation and speaking performance test with an analytical rubric collected the data. The students’ speaking performances increased from Cycle I (mean score = 65.5) to Cycle II (mean score = 74.45). Improvements related to better engagement in class activities, learner confidence and peer interactions. These findings suggest that, from an SLA perspective, debate activities enhance interaction by enabling learners to negotiate meaning and co-construct language during communicative exchanges. However, improvements in grammatical accuracy and vocabulary range were more limited. The findings indicate a 13.7% improvement in speaking performance, highlighting the pedagogical value of debate in enhancing communicative competence in EFL contexts.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 in Editing Arabic Writing: A Comparative Study With Human Editors
abstract: This study examines the accuracy of ChatGPT-4 in editing Arabic text as compared to human editors. Arabic language teachers and ChatGPT-4 edited a purposive sample of 25 texts written by freshmen, intermediate, and senior students at the Teaching Arabic Language Institute, Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University. Grammatical, lexical, spelling, and stylistic errors were categorized using an error taxonomy, and accuracy was assessed using precision, recall, F1-scores, and error reduction rates. In order to contextualize perceptions of AI versus human editing, learner feedback was also collected. Findings indicate that there is a strong correlation between human ratings and ChatGPT-4 in grammatical accuracy (ρ = 0.81), resulting in an effective reduction of surface-level errors. However, it underperformed human ratings in stylistic flow and lexical refinement. Students described ChatGPT-4’s editing as clear and simplified but often mechanical, while human-edited texts were reported as more natural and culturally meaningful. Inferential analyses confirmed significant differences between the two conditions in stylistic and lexical dimensions. These results suggest that ChatGPT-4 has

title: Mediation in AI-Assisted Experiential Language Learning: Extending TPACK Through the TPAEK Framework for Vietnamese as a Foreign Language Education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping language education through its capacity to generate linguistic and multimodal learning materials. In low-resource contexts such as Vietnamese as a Foreign Language (VFL), however, AI outputs may produce culturally generalized or inaccurate representations because culturally grounded training data remain uneven. This mixed-methods questionnaire study examines how 54 VFL teachers perceive the pedagogical usefulness, applicability, and ethical implications of GenAI in experiential language learning. Building on the limitations of TPACK, the study proposes the Technological–Pedagogical–AI Ethical Knowledge (TPAEK) framework as a context-sensitive analytical lens that treats ethical knowledge as a mediating dimension of pedagogical decision-making. Quantitative findings indicate positive perceptions of GenAI’s pedagogical value and applicability, whereas ethical awareness emerged as a distinct but not directly predictive dimension in this exploratory model. Open-ended responses identified recurrent teacher-reported forms of AI-induced cultural distortion, particularly cross-cultural blending, visual inaccuracy, cultural misinformat

title: Perezhivanie Through Peer Scaffolding in Academic Writing by Vietnamese University EFL Students
abstract: The process of academic writing in English does not only present linguistic and cognitive problems to Vietnamese EFL university students, but also overwhelming emotional pressures. This qualitative case study is based on the Sociocultural Theory, but it focuses on the emergence and development of learners’ perezhivanie, or integrated emotional-cognitive experience, with peer scaffolding in pre-writing, while-writing, and post-writing stages in a Confucian Heritage Culture (CHC) environment. Classroom observation and semi-structured interviews with ten symmetrical peer dyads provided the data that were analyzed by adapting the peer scaffolding framework. The results show that there is a developmental process through anxiety and dependence into engagement, co-construction and finally to self-regulation. Although values such as harmony, face-saving and respect found in CHC would encourage affective safety, they also restrict cognitive challenge by reducing open dispute. This work contributes to the sociocultural research because it theorizes perezhivanie as culturally mediated in cooperative academic writing.

title: The Impact of Technology-Enhanced Edutainment on EFL Learners’ Speaking and Listening Skills: An Experimental Study
abstract: This paper examines how edutainment can be enhanced using technology and its effect on the acquisition of listening and speaking skills among learners of English as a Foreign Language (EFL). The researchers used a quasi-experimental design with two groups: an experimental group taught using technology-enhanced edutainment and a control group taught using traditional teaching methods. A sample of first-year female students (35 students per group, totaling 70) from a governmental school in Cairo, Egypt, was used. To measure the four major sub-skills (predicting, listening for gist, listening for specific information, and listening for details), the researcher created a Listening Skills Test and a Speaking Assessment Scale that included five main dimensions (accuracy, fluency and pronunciation, content relevance, interaction and communication, and appropriate vocabulary and expressions). The psychometric properties of the two instruments, including validity and reliability, were confirmed. These two instruments were employed as pre- and post-tests of the experimental and control groups. The SPSS-based analysis of the data revealed that the positive impact of technology-enhanced edutai

title: The Development of Virtual Reality-Based Virtual Tour Learning Media to Enhance Descriptive Writing Skills of Indonesian for Foreign Speakers
abstract: Indonesian language learning for foreign speakers (BIPA) has been experiencing significant growth and increasing interest. The rising number of BIPA learners presents challenges in providing learning media that are engaging, contextual, and effective. Virtual Reality (VR) technology offers opportunities to deliver immersive and interactive learning experiences. This study aimed to develop and examine the effectiveness of VR-based Virtual Tour learning media in improving BIPA students’ descriptive writing skills. The research employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation). The media were designed with visual, audio, and interactive elements, and validated through expert judgment. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was conducted with 30 BIPA students at Universitas Sebelas Maret. The experimental class used VR-based media, while the control class relied on conventional textbooks. Data were collected through performance tests, questionnaires, observations, and interviews. Findings revealed that the experimental class achieved a higher average score (M = 75.2) than the cont

title: Ideational Meaning-Making in Vietnamese English-Medium Medical Research Articles: A Systemic Functional Linguistics Perspective
abstract: English-medium medical research writing plays an increasingly important role in the circulation of biomedical knowledge among Vietnamese scholars. While previous Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL) research has examined individual grammatical resources such as transitivity or nominalisation, less attention has been paid to how ideational resources align across research-article sections. This study investigates the ideational organisation of Vietnamese English-medium medical research articles through a corpus-based SFL analysis of Abstract and Discussion sections from 40 articles published in Vietnam-based medical journals. The analysis examines process types, agency in Material clauses, and nominalisation as interrelated resources shaping the construal of biomedical experience and causality. The findings reveal a stable action–classification core dominated by Material and Relational processes, pervasive non-human agency, and intensified nominalisation in Discussions. By modelling these patterns as a section-sensitive ideational configuration, the study demonstrates how clause-level grammatical resources align to construe biomedical knowledge as impersonal, mechanism-oriented, and

title: Beyond the Slipper: A Textual and Intercultural Analysis of Folk Justice and Moral Closure in Tấm Cám and Grimm’s “Cinderella” / Aschenputtel
abstract: This article offers a textual and intercultural analysis of Tấm Cám and Grimm’s “Cinderella” / Aschenputtel, with particular attention to folk justice, punishment, moral closure, and critical cultural awareness. While both tales are commonly situated within the Cinderella-type tradition, motif-based comparison alone cannot fully explain how they produce different moral effects. Drawing on Byram’s notions of interpreting and relating and critical cultural awareness, the study reads the two tales as culturally situated moral narratives rather than as simple variants of a universal plot. Through close textual reading and ICC-informed interpretation, the article shows that both narratives begin with a persecuted heroine whose suffering is located within the household and whose virtue is supported by supernatural assistance. However, Aschenputtel moves toward justice through recognition, exposure, and symbolic punishment, whereas Tấm Cám imagines justice through repeated loss, transformation, return, and retributive closure. The analysis argues that the two tales share a Cinderella-type grammar but construct different models of moral imagination. By extending ICC-informed reading into c

title: Reception of Mashhur Zhusup Kopeyev’s Poetry by Modern Readers: An Empirical Study
abstract: This article examines the reception of Mashhur Zhusup Kopeyev’s poetry by modern readers from an empirical perspective. The study aims to determine how contemporary readers understand historical poetic texts, what emotional responses they experience, and how they interpret the social and moral meanings embedded in the poems. Several socially and morally oriented poetic excerpts by Mashhur Zhusup were used as research material. A total of 46 respondents participated in the survey. Participants evaluated the comprehensibility of the poems, their emotional impact, and their relevance to contemporary society, and also provided open-ended responses. In addition, the effects of Kazakh language proficiency, frequency of reading nineteenth-century literature, and perceived linguistic difficulty on text comprehension were statistically analyzed. The results showed that most respondents were able to identify the social criticism, moral ideas, and implicit meanings presented in the poems. A strong positive correlation was found between comprehension and emotional impact. The findings also demonstrate that historical poetry is frequently interpreted through the lens of contemporary issues such

title: Improving International Learners' Reading of Thai Royal Words Derived From Pali and Sanskrit: An Error Analysis and Instructional Intervention
abstract: This study aimed 1) to investigate reading errors in Thai royal words derived from Pali (PL) and Sanskrit (SKT) among first-year students enrolled in the Communicative Thai Language for Foreigners (TLF) Program at Kasetsart University and 2) to develop and evaluate an instructional intervention designed to improve their reading ability. The participants were 10 international students enrolled in the course 01363132 Thai Reading II during the second semester of the academic year 2025, selected through purposive sampling. Research instruments included Thai royal words reading exercises, instructional materials containing Pali and Sanskrit-derived royal words, and oral reading tasks. Data were collected through three instructional cycles and analyzed using descriptive statistics and repeated-measures ANOVA. The findings revealed four major categories of reading errors: consonant cluster reduction (36.7%), final consonant insertion (26.5%), incorrect reading of Samāsa compounds (20.4%), and misreading of Pali and Sanskrit-derived spellings (16.3%). These difficulties were associated with limited phonological awareness, insufficient morphological awareness, and cross-linguistic influenc

title: Exploring EFL Writing Assessment in Omani Higher Education: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models and Human Raters
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of three automated assessors—ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini—in evaluating English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing tasks across four foundation levels. The design was quantitative and comparative. It compared human ratings with AI-generated scores for two types of writing tasks. The evaluation was based on a rubric covering Task Achievement, Coherence and Cohesion, Grammar, and Lexical Resource. The participants were 36 EFL learners enrolled in the General Foundation Program at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences, Oman. Writing scores were analyzed using SPSS to identify differences between human and AI writing assessments. Results indicate that ChatGPT and DeepSeek closely align with human ratings at lower proficiency levels (Levels 1 and 2). However, discrepancies emerged at Level 4, especially in Coherence and Cohesion, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Lexical Resource. Gemini showed limited reliability and inconsistent alignment across all levels. The findings suggest that automated tools can support the assessment of simpler writing tasks. However, human raters remain essential for evaluating more complex language us

title: Errors Committed by Jordanian Undergraduate SFL Students at Al al-Bayt University Regarding the Use of Passive Voice in Spanish
abstract: Due to the typical discrepancies between the formation of the passive voice in Spanish and Arabic, university students often make a number of errors when constructing passive voice sentences in Spanish. The current study seeks to locate these different kinds of errors, their underlying causes, and some ways to avoid them. Accordingly, thirty university students enrolled in the Spanish and English Program in a Jordanian public university were asked to take an assessment test in order to determine their errors committed when using the passive voice. It is found that most errors were related to morphological formation, gender and number agreement, and confusion between Spanish passive types. These errors have multiple causes and sources, such as Arabic influence and unfamiliarity with Spanish conjugation and tenses. Confusion between the passive types and gender and number agreement accounted for most errors. Accordingly, instructors should emphasize the special applications of the past participle in the periphrastic passive, which conveys gender and number. Besides, professors should consider the distinctions between the two kinds of passives and thoroughly go over the many tenses an

title: Digital Dialogues: Exploring Code-Switching and Language Innovation Among Gen Z on Social Media
abstract: This study investigates patterns of code-switching, slang usage, and digital language innovation among Generation Z within Indonesian social media contexts, focusing on interactions on Instagram, TikTok, and Twitter. Drawing on sociolinguistic and digital discourse perspectives, the research examines how Gen Z constructs meaning, expresses identity, and negotiates social relationships through hybrid language practices that combine Indonesian, English, localized slang, abbreviations, emojis, and non-standard spellings. The study employs a qualitative research design with thematic analysis as the framework for data analysis, supported by participant comparison to capture the multifaceted and multimodal nature of online communication. The findings reveal that digital language use among Gen Z promotes emotional expressiveness, communicative efficiency, and peer solidarity, functioning as a key mechanism for identity formation and group affiliation. However, the results also indicate potential challenges, including tone ambiguity, misinterpretation, and the blurring of boundaries between informal digital registers and formal academic language. These issues are particularly relevant in b

title: Reader Reception of Cultural and Intertextual Codes in Selected Contemporary Kazakh Literature
abstract: This study investigates the reception of cultural and intertextual codes by readers in contemporary Kazakh literature. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating quantitative and qualitative analyses. Empirical data were collected through an online survey involving 138 participants, comprising Likert-scale items and open-ended interpretive responses designed to assess recognition of historical, mythological, and symbolic references in literary texts. Quantitative data were analyzed using R software, including descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s Alpha, factor analysis, correlation analysis, and ANOVA. Results indicate strong positive correlations between the understanding of cultural codes, recognition of intertextual elements, and interpretation of historical-mythological references. Factor analysis confirmed that cultural-intertextual understanding forms a unified cognitive construct, while qualitative analysis revealed that participants interpret literary texts through mythological, historical, symbolic, and emotional frameworks. No statistically significant differences were found between reading frequency and levels of cultural-intertextual comprehension. Findings

title: Bridging Narratology and Stylistics: Focalization Through Foregrounding in the Arabic Translation of The Book Thief
abstract: Markus Zusak’s The Book Thief is renowned for its thematic engagement with the power of words. It is stylistically marked by a narrative form in which the narrator, Death, frequently merges with the characters’ perspectives, providing an ideal framework for investigating focalization in translation. This blending produces a complex form of focalization that necessitates a combined narratological and stylistic analysis to evaluate its textual survival across languages. Drawing on Genette’s (1980) differentiation between “who speaks” and “who sees,” this study conceptualizes focalization as a form of narrative coloring. Grounded in Leech and Short’s (2007) stylistic framework, this study focuses specifically on Rimmon-Kenan’s (2002) facets of focalization, psychological and ideological dimensions, proposing that these are most clearly realized through foregrounding. Adopting a comparative close-reading approach, the study examines how these stylistic features serve as diagnostic cues for inferring focalization and evaluates their rendering in the Arabic translation, where translation emerges not as a neutral transfer of content, but as a reconfiguration of this stylistic and interpre

title: Rhetorical Construction of Charismatic Leadership: A Discourse Analysis of King Abdullah II’s Political Speeches
abstract: The study seeks to understand how King Abdullah II of Jordan employs various rhetorical strategies to project his authority and establish a leadership image that blends historical traditions with openness to progressive approaches. The paper uses a qualitative methodology to analyze a carefully selected sample of the King's speeches delivered between 2019 and 2024, drawing upon the three elements of Aristotelian rhetoric: morality, emotion, and reason. The analysis focused on how these elements are integrated to construct an impactful discourse capable of establishing legitimacy, persuading the public, guiding public policy, and fostering international cooperation. The study's findings showed that the King's discourse is centered on the promotion of morality and legitimacy through references to Hashemite history and religion, thereby enhancing the leadership's credibility and bolstering its image among the public. Emotion is also employed strategically to forge a human connection with the audience and reinforce national unity and shared belonging. This integration of the three rhetorical elements reveals a leadership personality rooted in tradition yet forward-looking, capable of i

title: Lexical Diversity, Structural Transformation, and Collocational Features in a Six-Language Parallel Subcorpus
abstract: This study analyzes lexical diversity, structural transformation, and collocational features based on a six-language parallel subcorpus consisting of Kazakh, English, Uzbek, Turkish, Uyghur, and Azerbaijani texts. The main objective of the research is to identify lexical and structural changes occurring during translation across the six languages using a corpus-based approach and to demonstrate the typological similarities among Turkic languages from a comparative perspective. A multilingual parallel corpus organized according to the principle of paragraph-level alignment was used as the research material. The corpus data were processed in the R programming environment, where lexical diversity analysis, structural transformation analysis, and bigram-based collocation analysis were conducted. To determine lexical diversity, total words, unique words, and type-token ratio (TTR) values were calculated. Structural transformations were identified through three translation models: expansion, compression, and stable structures. In addition, collocation structures across the languages were compared through bigram analysis. The results demonstrated relatively high lexical diversity indicato

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Analyze Linguistic Features in Literary Texts and Its Application in the Teaching Process
abstract: This article explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies for analyzing linguistic features in literary texts and their application in the teaching process. To achieve this objective, two novels–The Last Duty by A. Nurpeisov and Zharmak by M. Magauin–are selected as primary materials, and the methods and advantages of their analysis using AI tools are demonstrated. Traditional literary language analysis is typically based on manual interpretation and experience-driven judgment, which leads to several limitations such as low efficiency, high subjectivity, insufficient quantitative assessment, and limited scalability. Modern AI-based approaches–including natural language processing, language models, and knowledge graphs–help address these challenges. These technologies enable the accurate identification of linguistic features in literary texts, their quantitative evaluation, visualization, and comparative analysis. The article systematically examines the technical foundations and analytical criteria of AI in literary language analysis. Based on teaching experience, an AI-supported learning model is proposed, consisting of the stages: “before the lesson – during the l

title: Reflective Practice as a Professional Development Tool: Insights From EFL Teachers in Saudi Higher Education
abstract: Reflective Practice (RP) is widely recognised as one of the most prominent professional features that distinguishes a successful teacher. However, RP is a multifaceted concept for which even field scholars lack a unified definition of its procedures and meaning, potentially impacting practitioners’ perceptions and effective implementation. This exploratory study investigates how English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instructors in Saudi higher education perceive, understand, and use Reflective Practice (RP) for Professional Development (PD), using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with eight EFL instructors were subjected to thematic analysis, which was followed and complemented by quantitative data from the survey of 101 EFL instructors. Findings indicated that although instructors report positive perceptions of RP as professional development and awareness of its core principles, tools, and procedures, this knowledge rarely translates into systematic implementation. The study recommends cultivating an RP culture and promoting reflective communities among EFL instructors by implementing consistent, well-structured PD prog

title: Pragmatic Functions of Cooking Verb Metaphors in Kazakh and English: A Contrastive Study
abstract: Despite significant research interest in the semantics of culinary verbs in Kazakh and English, their pragmatic potential, particularly in comparative contexts, remains understudied, making this study relevant. The aim of this study is to identify metaphorical patterns and pragmatic functions of verbs denoting the thermal processing of food in two languages reflecting fundamentally different cultural and economic systems. The study was conducted within the framework of a cognitive-pragmatic approach. The material for the analysis comprised 130 metaphorical utterances, drawn from 12 Kazakh and 32 English verbs denoting cooking methods and actions, extracted from the Qazcorpus, Qazcorpora, Sozdikkor, and Farlex and Reverso dictionaries. The analysis revealed that culinary metaphors in both languages form a stable conceptual network, confirming the universal nature of metaphor as a cognitive mechanism. At the same time, significant cross-linguistic differences were identified: the emotional sphere dominates in Kazakh (56%), while contexts of social interaction and deception predominate in English (61%). title: Orthographic Norm and Linguistic Consciousness in the Kazakh Language: A Survey-Based Study of User Acceptance of Competing Variants
abstract: This article examines the acceptance of competing orthographic variants in the Kazakh language and discusses their relationship to language norms. The study aims to determine the extent to which language users support orthographic variants proposed by scholars who have criticized the current orthographic dictionary and to explore attitudes toward orthographic norms. The research is based on orthographic variants discussed in the works of O. Zhubay, A. Salkynbai, and B. Kapalbek. Data were collected through a Google Forms survey involving 92 respondents. The questionnaire included 30 pairs of competing orthographic variants and 12 statements designed to assess attitudes toward orthography. The data were analyzed using the R statistical software package. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, Welch’s t-test, and Cronbach’s alpha coefficient were employed. The results indicate that variants such as birdeñe (“бірдеңе”), alai-dülei (“алай-дүлей”), erkek-shora (“еркек-шора”), jeku (“жеку”), ärtis (“әртіс”), and jädigöi (“жәдігөй”) received relatively high levels of support. title: The Role of English for Specific Purposes (ESP) in Promoting Environmental Sustainability and Addressing Basic Societal Needs: Perspectives of University Teachers in Saudi Arabia
abstract: This study explores the role of English for Specific Purposes (ESP) in facilitating environmental sustainability and fulfilling basic societal needs from the perspective of university teachers in Saudi Arabia. Based on the principles of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) and Saudi Vision 2030, the study investigates the extent to which themes of sustainability are embedded in ESP curricula, teaching practices, institutional support mechanisms and perceived student outcomes. The research approach was quantitative and data were collected by a structured questionnaire from 30 ESP teachers working in Saudi higher education institutions. Descriptive statistical analysis showed high level of integration of sustainability into ESP curriculum (M = 4.05), effective assimilation of social requirements in language education (M = 4.03) and widespread application of sustainability pedagogical approaches (M = 4.05). Teachers reported high awareness and confidence in delivering sustainability-related curriculum (M = 3.97), but there was a marked gap in sustainability-focused professional training. title: Negotiating Tensions: Teacher Cognition, Student Feedback and Teacher Agency in an EFL Translation Classroom
abstract: Teacher cognition develops through multiple sources, yet less is known about how student feedback is interpreted in relation to teachers’ cognition and instructional decisions. Drawing on sociocultural theory and an ecological perspective on teacher agency, this qualitative case study examines how an EFL translation teacher at a Chinese university interpreted, evaluated and responded to student feedback on her teaching. Data were collected over three months through teacher and student semi-structured interviews, classroom observations and stimulated recall interviews. The findings show that the teacher’s initial cognition provided the basis on which feedback was understood and evaluated. Rather than producing immediate and uniform change, student feedback functioned as a mediational resource that brought the tensions between the teacher’s established cognition and classroom realities into sharper view. The teacher then weighed this feedback against her existing beliefs, contextual constraints, and future-oriented concerns. title: Metonymic Reconstruction of Culture-Loaded Words: A Multidimensional Dynamic Constraint Model Based on English Translations of The True Story of Ah Q
abstract: Translation of culture-loaded metonymic expressions is influenced by both the cultural stance of the translator and pragmatic accessibility. Based on the two English translations of The True Story of Ah Q by Yang Xianyi and Julia Lovell, this paper studies socially and culturally metonymic expressions. It employs chi-square tests and binary logistic regression analysis to examine how these two factors influence translators’ choices of metonymic reconstruction strategies. The findings reveal that: (1) under conditions of low pragmatic accessibility, translators’ cultural stance exerts a significant main effect on strategy selection (Cramér’s V = 0.368, p = 0.001), with the source-language-oriented Yang Xianyi being 6.2 times more likely than Julia Lovell to adopt vehicle-retention strategies; (2) under conditions of high pragmatic accessibility, the two translators demonstrate complete strategic convergence; and (3) interaction analysis suggests that extreme cognitive resistance may function as a boundary condition that weakens the differentiating effect of subjective stance on strategy choice. title: Conceptual Metaphors With the Source Domain “Natural Disaster” in Healthcare Media Discourses on COVID-19: The Case of Vietnamese Online Newspapers
abstract: This study examines the metaphorical framework of “natural disaster” in health communication discourse on the COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnamese online newspapers. Drawing on correlations in human experience and on knowledge projections from the source domain to the target domain, this paper clarifies the mapping mechanisms between the two conceptual spaces of “natural disaster” and “COVID-19 pandemic.” The paper explains the mechanisms of transference and attribute projection between the source and target spaces in linguistic cognition. From the principle of partial mapping in conceptual metaphor theory, the paper elucidates the hierarchical nature of conceptual thinking through the emergence of two metaphors related to two common types of natural disasters, namely “earthquake” and “tsunami”, in health communication discourse about the pandemic. Metaphorizing the pandemic as a type of natural disaster also implies its severity and promotes defensive measures and actions, thereby enhancing public awareness of disease prevention as well as encouraging cooperation and compliance with government and health authority regulations. title: Exploring Pragmatic Strategies in English Media Discourse on Energy: A Scoping Review
abstract: This scoping review examines pragmatic and linguistic strategies employed in English-language media discourse on renewable energy in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with implications for critical media literacy. A corpus of 450 media articles published between 2022 and 2024 was analyzed using a pragmatic framework focusing on speech acts, modality, hedging, stance markers, and framing strategies. Quantitative findings reveal that declaratives constitute 68% of evaluative statements, interrogatives 12%, and directives 20%. Epistemic modal expressions appear in 35% of predictions concerning renewable energy outcomes, while deontic modals account for 42% of prescriptive statements. Hedging devices are identified in 18% of evaluative claims, functioning to mitigate epistemic commitment. Positive stance markers are present in 54% of the articles, compared to 21% for negative stance markers. Qualitative analysis further demonstrates that media texts deploy face-saving strategies and nationalist discourse framing to construct renewable energy as both a civic obligation and a national strategic vision. title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in English for Specific Purposes Instruction: A Systematic Review of Trends, Outcomes, and Challenges (2022–2025)
abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence integration in English for Specific Purposes education since 2022 demands a thorough analysis of new developments, educational results, and implementation barriers. An evaluation of AI usage in ESP teaching and learning through 70 peer-reviewed empirical studies published during January 2022 to March 2025 forms this systematic review. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 70 studies were selected. Research shows that large language models, including ChatGPT, GPT-3, and GPT-4, appeared in 46% of the analyzed studies. Grammar correction programs, adaptive learning platforms, and automated assessment solutions were among the tools currently used by educators at a rate of 21%, 18%, and 15%, respectively. Business English (37%) was the most popular domain, followed by English for Medical Purposes (22%), English for Engineering (21%), and Technical English (Engineering and IT) (20%). The analyzed research papers revealed positive learner outcomes in 82% of the studies, particularly in core language skills. title: The Use of Non-Verbal Communication Channels Among Arabic Language Teachers in Government-Aided Religious Schools (GARS)
abstract: Communication plays an important role in the field of education, as it is one of the primary modes of interaction that occurs between teachers and students, especially during the teaching process. The use of appropriate and strategic verbal or non-verbal communication media can positively impact the teaching and learning process. However, verbal communication channels have received greater focus among researchers. Non-verbal communication is also important, as it can influence the extent of information imparted; teachers’ failure to apply it can hinder the teaching process. Accordingly, this study aimed to identify the level of non-verbal communication employed in Arabic language instruction across ten channels: physical appearance, kinesics, chronemics, haptics, facial expressions, oculesics, proxemics, paralinguistics, artefactual, and olfactory. This survey study was conducted with 356 students using simple random sampling at nine selected Government-Aided Religious Schools in Selangor. title: The Effects of Task-Based Language Teaching Assisted by Technology-Enhanced Reading Instruction on Reading Comprehension and Motivational Engagement of Chinese University Students
abstract: English reading is challenging for many Chinese university students, but conventional reading instruction often provides insufficient opportunities for active engagement, scaffolded support, and meaningful reading practice. Using a two-phase mixed-methods design, this study developed and evaluated a needs-based model of Task-Based Language Teaching assisted by Technology-Enhanced Reading Instruction (TBLT-TERI) for university-level EFL reading instruction in China. In Phase One, questionnaire responses from 357 non-English-major students and interviews with three College English teachers were used to identify learner needs, instructional considerations, and design principles for the model. In Phase Two, the model was implemented in a five-week quasi-experimental study involving two intact first-year classes (n = 64; 32 experimental, 32 control). title: Translator’s Creative Treason in a Textless Back-Translation of The Joy Luck Club
abstract: This study examines the manifestation of translator’s creative treason in a selected Chinese textless back-translation version of The Joy Luck Club by identifying and classifying three types of translator’s creative treason: individualized translation, mistranslation and omission, and abridged translation and trans-editing. It further examines the patterns of linguistic and cultural return in the target text of The Joy Luck Club. Guided by Toury’s (2012) discovery procedure, the study adopts a qualitative research design and conducts a comparative analysis based on a parallel corpus. The findings reveal notable differences among the three types of translator’s creative treason in the target text. Although the target text foregrounds a unidirectional pattern of cultural return in all three types of translator’s creative treason, the linguistic pattern is bidirectional, which further attenuates linguistic hybridity in the textless back-translation version of The Joy Luck Club.

title: Individualism, Power Distance, and Pronouns: A Cross-Cultural Comparison of Rhetorical Variation in EFL Essays
abstract: Recent research has suggested that cultural values such as power distance and individualism have an influence on the expression of rhetoric. While insightful, this research was conducted in only eight cultural contexts in Asia, limiting generalizability of the results. To expand our understanding of cultural influences on rhetoric, argumentative essays from 30 different EFL contexts that spanned multiple continents were evaluated from the International Corpus of Learner English (ICLE). Different pronouns and determiners from the essays were tallied and statistically compared to cultural values for power distance and individualism. Results revealed several significant relationships. Whereas first-person singular pronouns and determiners (e.g., “I”) tended to be used more by learners with individualistic cultural beliefs, first- and third-person plural pronouns and determiners (e.g., “we” and “they”) tended to be used more in collective societies with higher power distance. Results also revealed that proficiency and gender explained some of the variance in how pronouns or determiners were used.
